newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Head of breakaway Karabakh named Armenian PM.
newsitem.headline: Head of breakaway Karabakh named Armenian PM.

text.p: President Levon Ter-Petrosyan appointed the leader of the self-proclaimed Nagorno-Karabakh republic, Robert Kocharyan, to the post of Armenian prime minister on Thursday.

Karabakh, populated mostly by Armenians but part of neighbouring Azerbaijan, fought a bitter war for independence from Baku in 1988 to 1994, seizing large parts of Azerbaijan proper. Fighting has stopped but there has been no political solution.

Thousands of people have been killed in the conflict between Azerbaijan and Karabakh which was unofficially but openly backed by Armenia. It was the first violent ethnic conflict in the former Soviet Union which also helped hasten its disintegration.
Kocharyan, 43, a former Communist Party official, was elected Karabakh president in 1996 and is a firm supporter of Karabakh independence.

Kocharyan's press secretary quoted Ter-Petrosyan as saying that such an appointment would serve the economic and security interests of both Armenia and Karabakh. No state has recognised Karabakh, though the territory effectively runs itself without any interference from Baku.
There was no immediate reaction from Azerbaijan.
